final_answer: George (Sir George) fears his country wife might become a “Fine Lady”—one who “lives all over the town rather than at home,” is driven by “the Lust of Conquest” and vanity, “loses the feelings of Wife and Mother in the whirl of dissipation,” is “virtuous…by chance,” and keeps her husband from ruin only by “her dexterity at the Card-Table.”

question: Why does Mr. Hardcastle want his daughter to meet Charles Marlow?
final_answer: Mr. Hardcastle wants his daughter to meet Charles Marlow because he has “pitched upon” Marlow as a suitable match: Marlow is “the son of my old friend, Sir Charles Marlow,” and Hardcastle has heard he is well educated (“bred a scholar”), intended for public service, and “a man of an excellent understanding.”
